question: After the no-op pacing defect is fixed, should ambiguous outbound rows with no reconciliation-capable adapter remain pending without consuming retry budget instead of aging to failed?
rationale: That behavior is a deliberate recovery tradeoff: it improves future recoverability but changes how existing ambiguous rows behave after upgrade and can leave operator-visible pending entries until a reconciler or manual action exists.

options.title: Accept pending deferral after repair
options.body: Merge this direction once unavailable-reconciler deferrals no longer consume replay pacing and exact-head validation is green.

options.title: Keep terminal failure as default
options.body: Reject this PR direction and require a separate product path for surfacing or reconciling ambiguous rows before preserving them indefinitely.

options.title: Defer to broader ledger design
options.body: Pause this PR and leave the behavior to the broader delivery-ledger work tracked by the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Accept pending deferral after repair
recommendation.body: Merge this direction once unavailable-reconciler deferrals no longer consume replay pacing and exact-head validation is green.

likelyOwner.reason: The durable outbound lifecycle and recovery contract history points most strongly to this owner for the recovery tradeoff.
